title: Coherent cohomology of a smooth projective curve over an algebraically closed field
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let
$X$ be a smooth projective curve
over $k$, and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module.
Then $H^i(X,\mathcal F)$ is a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space for
$i=0,1$, and vanishes for $i\ge2$.

proof.text:
By [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve], $X$ is a projective curve over
$k$, and $k$, being algebraically closed, is infinite. So by
[lem-pc-projective-curve-finite-projection] we may choose a finite
(in particular affine) morphism $u:X\to\mathbf P^1_k$. If
$W=\operatorname{Spec}(R)\subset\mathbf P^1_k$ is affine, then
$u^{-1}(W)=\operatorname{Spec}(B)$ with $B$ finite over $R$.
The restriction of $\mathcal F$ is $\widetilde M$ for a finite
$B$-module $M$: this is the affine characterization of coherence on
the locally Noetherian scheme $X$ in
[pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. Since $B$ is finite over $R$, the
finite set of $B$-generators of $M$ also generates $M$ over $R$. For a
principal open $D(f)\subset W$, its inverse image is
$\operatorname{Spec}(B_f)$ and the sections are $M_f$, with restriction
map the usual localization map. Thus $u_*\mathcal F|_W=\widetilde M$
with $M$ finite over $R$, and these local descriptions show that
$u_*\mathcal F$ is coherent.

For every affine $W\subset\mathbf P^1_k$, its inverse image is affine;
therefore higher cohomology of $\mathcal F$ on $u^{-1}(W)$ vanishes by
[pqf-lem-affine-vanishing]. On this affine base,
[lem-pc-cohomology-sections-affine-base] identifies
$\Gamma(W,R^q u_*\mathcal F)$ with
$H^q(u^{-1}(W),\mathcal F)$, so these sections vanish for every
$q>0$ and every affine $W$. Since affine opens form a basis of
$\mathbf P^1_k$, $R^q u_*\mathcal F=0$ for $q>0$. The Leray spectral
sequence from [pqf-lem-leray] therefore degenerates to canonical
isomorphisms

$$
H^i(X,\mathcal F)\cong H^i(\mathbf P^1_k,u_*\mathcal F).
$$

The right side is finite-dimensional for $i=0,1$ by
[lem-sc-p1-coherent-finite], and is zero for $i\ge2$ by
[lem-sc-p1-hi-vanishing]. This proves all assertions.
